### The important point\
\
This **does not necessarily mean every JSP has a different error**.\

- An error in `navbar.jsp` or `footer.jsp` (every page includes them).\
- A missing servlet mapping or imported class.\
- One model class (such as `User` or `CartView`) not compiling.\
- A project build-path or Maven dependency problem.\

Since **all pages are affected at once**, I don't think each JSP has an independent bug.\

# ✅ Correction 1 (Important)\
\
The audit changes:\
\
```jsp\
\u003cform action=\\"${pageContext.request.contextPath}/payment\\"\
      method=\\"post\\"\u003e\
```\
\
This is fine **only because** it also adds:\
\
```java\
@Override\
protected void doPost(...)\
{\
    doGet(request, response);\
}\
```\
\
to `PaymentServlet`.\
\
Otherwise, a **405 Method Not Allowed** error would occur.\
\
So if you use **POST** from `checkout.jsp`, **keep the `doPost()` method** in `PaymentServlet`.\
\
✔ I agree with this change.\
\
---\
\
# ✅ Correction 2 (Even More Important)\
\
The audit says:\
\
```jsp\
\u003cinput type=\\"hidden\\"\
       name=\\"address\\"\
       value=\\"\u003c%= request.getParameter(\\"address\\") %\u003e\\"\u003e\
```\
\
This works.\
\
However, **I recommend passing all checkout fields**, not only the address.\
\
For example:\
\
```jsp\
\u003cinput type=\\"hidden\\" name=\\"address\\"\
       value=\\"\u003c%=request.getParameter(\\"address\\")%\u003e\\"\u003e\
\
\u003cinput type=\\"hidden\\" name=\\"city\\"\
       value=\\"\u003c%=request.getParameter(\\"city\\")%\u003e\\"\u003e\
\
\u003cinput type=\\"hidden\\" name=\\"state\\"\
       value=\\"\u003c%=request.getParameter(\\"state\\")%\u003e\\"\u003e\
\
\u003cinput type=\\"hidden\\" name=\\"pincode\\"\
       value=\\"\u003c%=request.getParameter(\\"pincode\\")%\u003e\\"\u003e\
```\
\
Even if your current `PlaceOrderServlet` only stores the address, this keeps the payment page ready for future enhancements.\

# Step 2\
\
## Update `PaymentServlet.java`\
\
Since the checkout page already collected all the customer information, the payment page should simply let the user choose a payment method.\
\
Your `PaymentServlet` remains:\
\
```java\
@WebServlet(\\"/payment\\")\

\
    @Override\
    protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest request,\
                         HttpServletResponse response)\
            throws ServletException, IOException {\
\
        request.getRequestDispatcher(\\"/WEB-INF/views/payment.jsp\\")\
               .forward(request, response);\
\
    }\
\
}\
```\

## ❌ Current Flow (Not Correct)\
\
```text\
Checkout\
      │\
      ▼\
PlaceOrderServlet\
      │\
      ▼\
Order Created\
      │\
      ▼\
Orders Page\
```\
\
Then we added:\
\
```text\
PaymentServlet\
payment.jsp\
```\
\
But **nothing calls `PaymentServlet`**.\
\
So currently the Payment module is **disconnected**.\
\
---\
\
# ✅ Correct Flow\
\
A real e-commerce flow should be:\
\
```text\
Cart\
      │\
      ▼\
Checkout\
      │\
      ▼\
Payment\
      │\
      ▼\
Place Order\
      │\
      ▼\
Orders\
```\
\
That means:\
\
```text\
checkout.jsp\
```\
\
should **redirect to**\
\
```text\
/payment\
```\
\
instead of directly calling\
\
```text\
/place-order\
```\
\
Then\
\
```text\
payment.jsp\
```\
\
should submit to\
\
```text\
/place-order\
```\
\
passing the selected payment method.\
\
---\
\
# We need to change only TWO files\
\
## 1️⃣ checkout.jsp\
\
Change\
\
```jsp\
\u003cform action=\\"${pageContext.request.contextPath}/place-order\\"\
      method=\\"post\\"\u003e\
```\
\
to\
\
```jsp\
\u003cform action=\\"${pageContext.request.contextPath}/payment\\"\
      method=\\"get\\"\u003e\
```\
\
---\
\
## 2️⃣ payment.jsp\
\
Change\
\
```jsp\
\u003cform action=\\"${pageContext.request.contextPath}/payment-success\\"\
      method=\\"post\\"\u003e\
```\
\
to\
\
```jsp\
\u003cform action=\\"${pageContext.request.contextPath}/place-order\\"\
      method=\\"post\\"\u003e\
```\
\
---\
\
# Why?\
\
Because **PlaceOrderServlet** already creates the order.\
\
There is **no need** for another `PaymentSuccessServlet`.\
\
For an internship-level project:\
\
```text\
Checkout\
     │\
     ▼\
Payment\
     │\
     ▼\
PlaceOrderServlet\
     │\
     ▼\
Orders\
```\
\
is clean MVC and sufficient.\
\

## Complete Code\

```java\
package com.fashionstore.controller;\
\
import java.io.IOException;\
\
import com.fashionstore.dao.UserDAO;\
import com.fashionstore.dao.impl.UserDAOImpl;\
import com.fashionstore.model.User;\
\
import jakarta.servlet.ServletException;\
import jakarta.servlet.annotation.WebServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpSession;\
\
@WebServlet(\\"/update-profile\\")\
public class UpdateProfileServlet extends HttpServlet {\
\
    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;\
\
    private UserDAO userDAO;\
\
    @Override\
    public void init() throws ServletException {\
\
        userDAO = new UserDAOImpl();\
\
    }\
\
    @Override\
    protected void doPost(HttpServletRequest request,\
                          HttpServletResponse response)\
            throws ServletException, IOException {\
\
        HttpSession session = request.getSession(false);\
\
        if (session == null ||\
                session.getAttribute(\\"loggedInUser\\") == null) {\
\
            response.sendRedirect(\
                    request.getContextPath() + \\"/login\\");\
\
            return;\
\
        }\
\
        User loggedInUser =\
                (User) session.getAttribute(\\"loggedInUser\\");\
\
        User user = new User();\
\
        user.setUserId(loggedInUser.getUserId());\
\
        user.setFullName(loggedInUser.getFullName());\
\
        user.setEmail(loggedInUser.getEmail());\
\
        user.setPassword(loggedInUser.getPassword());\
\
        user.setPhone(request.getParameter(\\"phone\\"));\
\
        user.setAddress(request.getParameter(\\"address\\"));\
\
        user.setCity(request.getParameter(\\"city\\"));\
\
        user.setState(request.getParameter(\\"state\\"));\
\
        user.setPincode(request.getParameter(\\"pincode\\"));\
\
        boolean updated =\
                userDAO.updateUser(user);\
\
        if (updated) {\
\
            session.setAttribute(\\"loggedInUser\\", user);\
\
        }\
\
        response.sendRedirect(\
                request.getContextPath() + \\"/profile\\");\
\
    }\
\
}\
```\
\

## Complete Code\

```java\
package com.fashionstore.controller;\
\
import java.io.IOException;\
\
import com.fashionstore.dao.UserDAO;\
import com.fashionstore.dao.impl.UserDAOImpl;\
import com.fashionstore.model.User;\
\
import jakarta.servlet.ServletException;\
import jakarta.servlet.annotation.WebServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpSession;\
\
@WebServlet(\\"/profile\\")\
public class ProfileServlet extends HttpServlet {\
\
    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;\
\
    private UserDAO userDAO;\
\
    @Override\
    public void init() throws ServletException {\
\
        userDAO = new UserDAOImpl();\
\
    }\
\
    @Override\
    protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest request,\
                         HttpServletResponse response)\
            throws ServletException, IOException {\
\
        HttpSession session = request.getSession(false);\
\
        if (session == null ||\
            session.getAttribute(\\"loggedInUser\\") == null) {\
\
            response.sendRedirect(\
                    request.getContextPath() + \\"/login\\");\
            return;\
\
        }\
\
        User loggedInUser =\
                (User) session.getAttribute(\\"loggedInUser\\");\
\
        User user =\
                userDAO.getUserById(loggedInUser.getUserId());\
\
        request.setAttribute(\\"user\\", user);\
\
        request.getRequestDispatcher(\
                \\"/WEB-INF/views/profile.jsp\\")\
                .forward(request, response);\
\
    }\
\
}\
```\

## Complete Code\

```java\
package com.fashionstore.controller;\
\
import java.io.IOException;\
import java.util.List;\
\
import com.fashionstore.dao.OrderDAO;\
import com.fashionstore.dao.impl.OrderDAOImpl;\
import com.fashionstore.model.Order;\
import com.fashionstore.model.User;\
\
import jakarta.servlet.ServletException;\
import jakarta.servlet.annotation.WebServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpSession;\
\
@WebServlet(\\"/orders\\")\
public class OrdersServlet extends HttpServlet {\
\
    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;\
\
    private OrderDAO orderDAO;\
\
    @Override\
    public void init() throws ServletException {\
\
        orderDAO = new OrderDAOImpl();\
\
    }\
\
    @Override\
    protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest request,\
                         HttpServletResponse response)\
            throws ServletException, IOException {\
\
        HttpSession session = request.getSession(false);\
\
        if (session == null ||\
                session.getAttribute(\\"loggedInUser\\") == null) {\
\
            response.sendRedirect(\
                    request.getContextPath() + \\"/login\\");\
\
            return;\
\
        }\
\
        User user =\
                (User) session.getAttribute(\\"loggedInUser\\");\
\
        List\u003cOrder\u003e orders =\
                orderDAO.getOrdersByUserId(user.getUserId());\
\
        request.setAttribute(\\"orders\\", orders);\
\
        request.getRequestDispatcher(\
                \\"/WEB-INF/views/orders.jsp\\")\
                .forward(request, response);\
\
    }\
\
}\
```\

        │\
        ▼\
Check Login\
        │\
        ▼\
Get User ID\
        │\
        ▼\
Fetch Orders\
        │\
        ▼\
Send List\u003cOrder\u003e to JSP\
        │\
        ▼\
orders.jsp\
```\

## 🔥 Before we continue\
\
I noticed something important while reviewing the project.\
\
Your `Order` model only contains **order-level information** (order ID, total amount, status, date, etc.).\
\
So **`orders.jsp`** can currently display:\
\
- ✅ Order ID\
- ✅ Order Date\
- ✅ Total Amount\
- ✅ Payment Method\
- ✅ Status\
\
It **cannot display product names, images, or quantities** unless we retrieve the corresponding `OrderItem` records (and possibly join with `Product`/`ProductVariant`).\
\
### My recommendation\

5. Does ProductVariant contain enough info for PlaceOrderServlet?\\r\
NO, it does not. The ProductVariant model contains variantId, productId, size, and stock, but it completely lacks price information. This is because in your database schema, price is stored at the Product level, not the ProductVariant level.\\r\

6. How PlaceOrderServlet should correctly obtain the price\\r\
PlaceOrderServlet should NOT attempt to fetch the price using ProductVariantDAO.\\r\
\\r\
Instead, the servlet should call cartItemDAO.getCartView(cartId). This method returns a list of CartView objects. Because CartView was well-designed, it already contains the live price property. cartItemDAO.getCartView(cartId) Why: To fetch all items in the user's cart, ensuring the cart isn't empty, and to obtain the live product prices and requested quantities.\\r\

cartItemDAO.clearCart(cartId) Why: To empty the user's shopping cart now that checkout is successfully completed.\\r\

\\r\
What was missing?\\r\
The module was missing the ability to retrieve the generated Order ID after placing an order.\\r\
\\r\
The Exact Missing/Incorrect Method: The placeOrder(Order order) method in OrderDAO was returning a boolean.\\r\
\\r\
Why it is needed by PlaceOrderServlet: When the PlaceOrderServlet inserts a new order into the orders table, it absolutely needs the auto-generated primary key (order_id) returned by MySQL. Without this order_id, the servlet has no way to insert the associated cart items into the order_items table because order_id is a required foreign key.\\r\
\\r\
To fix this, we must use PreparedStatement.RETURN_GENERATED_KEYS to capture the ID and return an int instead of a boolean.\\r\
\\r\
(Note: I have already proactively corrected these files in your codebase using my tools, but here is the complete corrected code as requested).\\r\

package com.fashionstore.dao.impl;\\r\
import java.sql.Connection;\\r\
import java.sql.PreparedStatement;\\r\
import java.sql.ResultSet;\\r\
import java.sql.SQLException;\\r\
import java.util.ArrayList;\\r\
import java.util.List;\\r\
import com.fashionstore.dao.OrderDAO;\\r\
import com.fashionstore.model.Order;\\r\
import com.fashionstore.util.DBConnection;\\r\
public class OrderDAOImpl implements OrderDAO {\\r\
    // ===========================\\r\
    // SQL Queries\\r\
    // ===========================\\r\
    private static final String PLACE_ORDER_SQL =\\r\
            \\"INSERT INTO orders(user_id, total_amount, shipping_address, payment_method, status) VALUES(?,?,?,?,?)\\";\\r\
    private static final String GET_ORDER_BY_ID_SQL =\\r\
            \\"SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_id=?\\";\\r\
    private static final String GET_ORDERS_BY_USER_SQL =\\r\
            \\"SELECT * FROM orders WHERE user_id=? ORDER BY order_date DESC\\";\\r\
    private static final String GET_ALL_ORDERS_SQL =\\r\
            \\"SELECT * FROM orders ORDER BY order_date DESC\\";\\r\
    private static final String UPDATE_ORDER_STATUS_SQL =\\r\
            \\"UPDATE orders SET status=? WHERE order_id=?\\";\\r\
    private static final String CANCEL_ORDER_SQL =\\r\
            \\"UPDATE orders SET status='CANCELLED' WHERE order_id=?\\";\\r\
    private static final String DELETE_ORDER_SQL =\\r\
            \\"DELETE FROM orders WHERE order_id=?\\";\\r\
    @Override\\r\
    public int placeOrder(Order order) {\\r\
        try (Connection connection = DBConnection.getConnection();\\r\
             PreparedStatement preparedStatement = connection.prepareStatement(PLACE_ORDER_SQL, PreparedStatement.RETURN_GENERATED_KEYS)) {\\r\
            preparedStatement.setInt(1, order.getUserId());\\r\
            preparedStatement.setBigDecimal(2, order.getTotalAmount());\\r\
            preparedStatement.setString(3, order.getShippingAddress());\\r\
            preparedStatement.setString(4, order.getPaymentMethod());\\r\
            preparedStatement.setString(5, order.getStatus());\\r\
            int affectedRows = preparedStatement.executeUpdate();\\r\
            \\r\
            if (affectedRows \u003e 0) {\\r\
                // Retrieve the auto-generated order_id\\r\
                try (ResultSet rs = preparedStatement.getGeneratedKeys()) {\\r\
                    if (rs.next()) {\\r\
                        return rs.getInt(1);\\r\
                    }\\r\
                }\\r\
            }\\r\
        } catch (SQLException e) {\\r\
            e.printStackTrace();\\r\
        }\\r\
        return 0; // Return 0 if insertion fails\\r\
    }\\r\
    @Override\\r\
    public Order getOrderById(int orderId) {\\r\
        try (Connection connection = DBConnection.getConnection();\\r\
             PreparedStatement preparedStatement = connection.prepareStatement(GET_ORDER_BY_ID_SQL)) {\\r\
            preparedStatement.setInt(1, orderId);\\r\
            ResultSet resultSet = preparedStatement.executeQuery();\\r\
            if (resultSet.next()) {\\r\
                return mapResultSetToOrder(resultSet);\\r\
            }\\r\
        } catch (SQLException e) {\\r\
            e.printStackTrace();\\r\
        }\\r\
        return null;\\r\

```java\
package com.fashionstore.controller;\
\
import java.io.IOException;\
import java.util.List;\
\
import com.fashionstore.dao.CartDAO;\
import com.fashionstore.dao.CartItemDAO;\
import com.fashionstore.dao.impl.CartDAOImpl;\
import com.fashionstore.dao.impl.CartItemDAOImpl;\
import com.fashionstore.model.Cart;\
import com.fashionstore.model.CartView;\
import com.fashionstore.model.User;\
\
import jakarta.servlet.ServletException;\
import jakarta.servlet.annotation.WebServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpSession;\
\
@WebServlet(\\"/checkout\\")\
public class CheckoutServlet extends HttpServlet {\
\
    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;\
\
    private CartDAO cartDAO;\
    private CartItemDAO cartItemDAO;\
\
    @Override\
    public void init() throws ServletException {\
\
        cartDAO = new CartDAOImpl();\
        cartItemDAO = new CartItemDAOImpl();\
\
    }\
\
    @Override\
    protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest request,\
                         HttpServletResponse response)\
            throws ServletException, IOException {\
\
        HttpSession session = request.getSession(false);\
\
        if (session == null || session.getAttribute(\\"loggedInUser\\") == null) {\
\
            response.sendRedirect(request.getContextPath() + \\"/login\\");\
            return;\
\
        }\
\
        User user = (User) session.getAttribute(\\"loggedInUser\\");\
\
        Cart cart = cartDAO.getCartByUserId(user.getUserId());\
\
        if (cart == null) {\
\
            response.sendRedirect(request.getContextPath() + \\"/cart\\");\
            return;\
\
        }\
\
        List\u003cCartView\u003e cartItems =\
                cartItemDAO.getCartView(cart.getCartId());\
\
        double total =\
                cartItemDAO.getCartTotal(cart.getCartId());\
\
        request.setAttribute(\\"cartItems\\", cartItems);\
        request.setAttribute(\\"cartTotal\\", total);\
\
        request.getRequestDispatcher(\\"/WEB-INF/views/checkout.jsp\\")\
               .forward(request, response);\
\
    }\
\
}\
```\
\

# What this servlet does\
\
✅ Checks whether the user is logged in.\
\
✅ Gets the user's cart.\
\
✅ Retrieves all cart items.\
\
✅ Calculates the total amount.\
\
✅ Opens `checkout.jsp`.\

```java id=\\"5j7u2x\\"\
package com.fashionstore.controller;\
\
import java.io.IOException;\
\
import com.fashionstore.dao.CartItemDAO;\
import com.fashionstore.dao.impl.CartItemDAOImpl;\
\
import jakarta.servlet.ServletException;\
import jakarta.servlet.annotation.WebServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;\
\
@WebServlet(\\"/remove-cart-item\\")\
public class RemoveCartItemServlet extends HttpServlet {\
\
    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;\
\
    private CartItemDAO cartItemDAO;\
\
    @Override\
    public void init() throws ServletException {\
\
        cartItemDAO = new CartItemDAOImpl();\
\
    }\
\
    @Override\
    protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest request,\
                         HttpServletResponse response)\
            throws ServletException, IOException {\
\
        String id = request.getParameter(\\"id\\");\
\
        if (id != null \u0026\u0026 !id.isEmpty()) {\
\
            int cartItemId = Integer.parseInt(id);\
\
            cartItemDAO.removeCartItem(cartItemId);\
\
        }\
\
        response.sendRedirect(request.getContextPath() + \\"/cart\\");\
\
    }\
\
}\
```\
\

# ✅ How it Works\
\
When the user clicks:\
\
```jsp id=\\"m2r1qk\\"\

    Remove\
\u003c/a\u003e\
```\
\
This servlet will:\
\
1. Read the `cartItemId`\
2. Delete the item from the `cart_items` table\
3. Redirect back to the Cart page\

## Complete Code\

```java\
package com.fashionstore.controller;\
\
import java.io.IOException;\
\
import com.fashionstore.dao.CartItemDAO;\
import com.fashionstore.dao.impl.CartItemDAOImpl;\
\
import jakarta.servlet.ServletException;\
import jakarta.servlet.annotation.WebServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;\
\
@WebServlet(\\"/update-cart\\")\
public class UpdateCartServlet extends HttpServlet {\
\
    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;\
\
    private CartItemDAO cartItemDAO;\
\
    @Override\
    public void init() throws ServletException {\
\
        cartItemDAO = new CartItemDAOImpl();\
\
    }\
\
    @Override\
    protected void doPost(HttpServletRequest request,\
                          HttpServletResponse response)\
            throws ServletException, IOException {\
\
        int cartItemId =\
                Integer.parseInt(request.getParameter(\\"cartItemId\\"));\
\
        int quantity =\
                Integer.parseInt(request.getParameter(\\"quantity\\"));\
\
        if (quantity \u003c 1) {\
\
            quantity = 1;\
\
        }\
\
        cartItemDAO.updateQuantity(cartItemId, quantity);\
\
        response.sendRedirect(request.getContextPath() + \\"/cart\\");\
\
    }\
\
}\
```\
\

# ✅ What this servlet does\
\
When the user clicks **Update** in `cart.jsp`:\
\
```jsp\
\u003cform action=\\"${pageContext.request.contextPath}/update-cart\\"\
      method=\\"post\\"\u003e\
```\
\
this servlet:\
\
- Reads `cartItemId`\
- Reads the new `quantity`\
- Updates the database\
- Redirects back to the cart page\

@WebServlet(\\"/cart\\")\

    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;\

\
    }\
\
    @Override\
    protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest request,\
                         HttpServletResponse response)\
            throws ServletException, IOException {\
\
        HttpSession session = request.getSession(false);\
\
        if (session == null || session.getAttribute(\\"loggedInUser\\") == null) {\
\
            response.sendRedirect(request.getContextPath() + \\"/login\\");\
            return;\
\
        }\
\
        User user = (User) session.getAttribute(\\"loggedInUser\\");\
\
        Cart cart = cartDAO.getCartByUserId(user.getUserId());\
\
        if (cart == null) {\
\
            cartDAO.createCart(user.getUserId());\
\
            cart = cartDAO.getCartByUserId(user.getUserId());\
\
        }\
\
        List\u003cCartView\u003e cartItems =\
                cartItemDAO.getCartView(cart.getCartId());\
\
        double total =\
                cartItemDAO.getCartTotal(cart.getCartId());\
\
        request.setAttribute(\\"cartItems\\", cartItems);\
\
        request.setAttribute(\\"cartTotal\\", total);\
\
        request.getRequestDispatcher(\\"/WEB-INF/views/cart.jsp\\")\
               .forward(request, response);\
\
    }\
\
    @Override\
    protected void doPost(HttpServletRequest request,\
                          HttpServletResponse response)\
            throws ServletException, IOException {\
\
        HttpSession session = request.getSession(false);\
\
        if (session == null || session.getAttribute(\\"loggedInUser\\") == null) {\
\
            response.sendRedirect(request.getContextPath() + \\"/login\\");\
            return;\
\
        }\
\
        User user = (User) session.getAttribute(\\"loggedInUser\\");\
\
        int variantId =\
                Integer.parseInt(request.getParameter(\\"variantId\\"));\
\
        int quantity =\
                Integer.parseInt(request.getParameter(\\"quantity\\"));\
\
        Cart cart =\
                cartDAO.getCartByUserId(user.getUserId());\
\
        if (cart == null) {\
\
            cartDAO.createCart(user.getUserId());\
\
            cart = cartDAO.getCartByUserId(user.getUserId());\
\
        }\
\
        int cartId = cart.getCartId();\
\
        if (cartItemDAO.isProductInCart(cartId, variantId)) {\
\
            CartItem item =\
                    cartItemDAO.getCartItem(cartId, variantId);\
\
            int newQuantity =\
                    item.getQuantity() + quantity;\
\
            cartItemDAO.updateQuantityByVariant(\
                    cartId,\
                    variantId,\
                    newQuantity);\
\
        } else {\
\
            CartItem item = new CartItem();\
\
            item.setCartId(cartId);\
\
            item.setVariantId(variantId);\
\
            item.setQuantity(quantity);\
\
            cartItemDAO.addToCart(item);\
\
        }\
\
        response.sendRedirect(request.getContextPath() + \\"/cart\\");\
\
    }\

## Before I generate `CartServlet.java`\
\
I found **one issue** in your project after reviewing everything we've built.\
\
Your current **Product Details page** sends:\
\
```jsp\
productId\
variantId\
quantity\
```\
\
But your **CartItem** stores only:\
\
```java\
cartId\
variantId\
quantity\
```\
\
which is correct.\
\
However, **to display the cart page**, we need additional product information like:\
\
- Product Name\
- Brand\
- Price\
- Image\
- Size\
- Quantity\
- Subtotal\
\
Your current `CartItem` model intentionally contains only IDs and quantity, so **the cart page cannot display product details using `CartItem` alone**. That means the next thing we build is **not the servlet first**—we need a query that joins:\
\
- `cart_items`\
- `product_variants`\
- `products`\
\
to retrieve the complete information for display.\
\
---\
\
## This is the correct order now\
\
1. **Create a `CartView` model (DTO)** to hold:\
   - product name\
   - brand\
   - image\
   - size\
   - price\
   - quantity\
   - subtotal\
\
2. Add one DAO method that returns `List\u003cCartView\u003e` using a JOIN query.\
\
3. Build `CartServlet.java`.\
\
4. Build `cart.jsp`.\
\
This keeps the rest of the module clean and avoids writing SQL in the servlet.\
\

# Module 8 : Authentication\
\
## Step 3 : `LogoutServlet.java`\
\
📁 **Location**\
\
```text\
src/main/java/com/fashionstore/controller/LogoutServlet.java\
```\
\
Create this file.\
\
```java\
package com.fashionstore.controller;\
\
import java.io.IOException;\
\
import jakarta.servlet.ServletException;\
import jakarta.servlet.annotation.WebServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpSession;\
\
@WebServlet(\\"/logout\\")\
public class LogoutServlet extends HttpServlet {\
\
    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;\
\
    @Override\
    protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest request,\
                         HttpServletResponse response)\
            throws ServletException, IOException {\
\
        HttpSession session = request.getSession(false);\
\
        if(session != null) {\
\
            session.invalidate();\
\
        }\
\
        response.sendRedirect(request.getContextPath() + \\"/login\\");\
\
    }\
\
}\
```\
\

# Module 8 : Authentication\
\
## Step 2 : `LoginServlet.java`\
\
📁 **Location**\
\
```text\
src/main/java/com/fashionstore/controller/LoginServlet.java\
```\
\
Create this file.\
\
```java\
package com.fashionstore.controller;\
\
import java.io.IOException;\
\
import com.fashionstore.dao.UserDAO;\
import com.fashionstore.dao.impl.UserDAOImpl;\
import com.fashionstore.model.User;\
\
import jakarta.servlet.ServletException;\
import jakarta.servlet.annotation.WebServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpSession;\
\
@WebServlet(\\"/login\\")\
public class LoginServlet extends HttpServlet {\
\
    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;\
\
    private UserDAO userDAO;\
\
    @Override\
    public void init() throws ServletException {\
\
        userDAO = new UserDAOImpl();\
\
    }\
\
    @Override\
    protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest request,\
                         HttpServletResponse response)\
            throws ServletException, IOException {\
\
        request.getRequestDispatcher(\\"/WEB-INF/views/login.jsp\\")\
               .forward(request, response);\
\
    }\
\
    @Override\
    protected void doPost(HttpServletRequest request,\
                          HttpServletResponse response)\
            throws ServletException, IOException {\
\
        String email = request.getParameter(\\"email\\");\
        String password = request.getParameter(\\"password\\");\
\
        User user = userDAO.loginUser(email, password);\
\
        if (user != null) {\
\
            HttpSession session = request.getSession();\
\
            session.setAttribute(\\"loggedInUser\\", user);\
\
            session.setAttribute(\\"userId\\", user.getUserId());\
\
            session.setAttribute(\\"userName\\", user.getFullName());\
\
            response.sendRedirect(request.getContextPath() + \\"/home\\");\
\
        } else {\
\
            request.setAttribute(\\"error\\",\
                    \\"Invalid Email or Password\\");\
\
            request.getRequestDispatcher(\\"/WEB-INF/views/login.jsp\\")\
                   .forward(request, response);\
\
        }\
\
    }\
\
}\
```\
\

\
```\

      ↓\

      ↓\
Redirect to Login\
      ↓\
User enters Email \u0026 Password\
      ↓\
UserDAOImpl.loginUser()\
      ↓\
Session Created\
      ↓\
Redirect to Home\
```\

# Step 3 : RegisterServlet.java\
\
**Location**\
\
```text\
FashionStore\
└── src\
    └── main\
        └── java\
            └── com\
                └── fashionstore\
                    └── controller\
                        └── RegisterServlet.java\
```\
\
Replace/create the file with the following code:\
\
```java\
package com.fashionstore.controller;\
\
import java.io.IOException;\
\
import com.fashionstore.dao.UserDAO;\
import com.fashionstore.dao.impl.UserDAOImpl;\
import com.fashionstore.model.User;\
\
import jakarta.servlet.ServletException;\
import jakarta.servlet.annotation.WebServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;\
\
@WebServlet(\\"/register\\")\
public class RegisterServlet extends HttpServlet {\
\
    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;\
\
    private UserDAO userDAO;\
\
    @Override\
    public void init() throws ServletException {\
\
        userDAO = new UserDAOImpl();\
\
    }\
\
    @Override\
    protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest request,\
                         HttpServletResponse response)\
            throws ServletException, IOException {\
\
        request.getRequestDispatcher(\\"/WEB-INF/views/register.jsp\\")\
               .forward(request, response);\
\
    }\
\
    @Override\
    protected void doPost(HttpServletRequest request,\
                          HttpServletResponse response)\
            throws ServletException, IOException {\
\
        String fullName = request.getParameter(\\"fullName\\");\
        String email = request.getParameter(\\"email\\");\
        String phone = request.getParameter(\\"phone\\");\
        String password = request.getParameter(\\"password\\");\
        String address = request.getParameter(\\"address\\");\
        String city = request.getParameter(\\"city\\");\
        String state = request.getParameter(\\"state\\");\
        String pincode = request.getParameter(\\"pincode\\");\
\
        // Email Validation\
        if (userDAO.emailExists(email)) {\
\
            request.setAttribute(\\"error\\",\
                    \\"Email already registered.\\");\
\
            request.getRequestDispatcher(\\"/WEB-INF/views/register.jsp\\")\
                   .forward(request, response);\
\
            return;\
\
        }\
\
        // Phone Validation\
        if (userDAO.phoneExists(phone)) {\
\
            request.setAttribute(\\"error\\",\
                    \\"Phone number already registered.\\");\
\
            request.getRequestDispatcher(\\"/WEB-INF/views/register.jsp\\")\
                   .forward(request, response);\
\
            return;\
\
        }\
\
        User user = new User();\
\
        user.setFullName(fullName);\
        user.setEmail(email);\
        user.setPhone(phone);\
        user.setPassword(password);\
        user.setAddress(address);\
        user.setCity(city);\
        user.setState(state);\
        user.setPincode(pincode);\
\
        boolean status = userDAO.registerUser(user);\
\
        if (status) {\
\
            response.sendRedirect(\
                    request.getContextPath() + \\"/login\\");\
\
        } else {\
\
            request.setAttribute(\\"error\\",\
                    \\"Registration Failed.\\");\
\
            request.getRequestDispatcher(\\"/WEB-INF/views/register.jsp\\")\
                   .forward(request, response);\
\
        }\
\
    }\
\
}\
```\

    private static final String ADD_TO_CART_SQL =\
            \\"INSERT INTO cart_items(cart_id, variant_id, quantity) VALUES(?,?,?)\\";\
\
    private static final String UPDATE_QUANTITY_SQL =\
            \\"UPDATE cart_items SET quantity=? WHERE cart_item_id=?\\";\

    private static final String UPDATE_QUANTITY_BY_VARIANT_SQL =\

\
import java.util.List;\
\
import com.fashionstore.model.CartItem;\
\
public interface CartItemDAO {\
\
    // Add Product To Cart\
    boolean addToCart(CartItem cartItem);\
\
    // Update Quantity Using Cart Item Id\
    boolean updateQuantity(int cartItemId, int quantity);\
\
    // Update Quantity Using Cart Id \u0026 Variant Id\
    boolean updateQuantityByVariant(int cartId, int variantId, int quantity);\

## ✅ What Changed?\
\
We added only **2 methods**:\
\
```java\
CartItem getCartItem(int cartId, int variantId);\
\
boolean updateQuantityByVariant(int cartId,\
                                int variantId,\
                                int quantity);\

\
These methods are required so that if the user adds the **same product** again:\
\
Instead of creating another row:\
\
```text\
Nike Shoes\
Qty : 1\
\
Nike Shoes\
Qty : 1\
```\
\
it becomes\
\
```text\
Nike Shoes\
Qty : 2\
```\
\
This is how every shopping cart behaves.\

\

## 🚨 The Problem\
\
When the user clicks **Add To Cart**, the servlet has to do this:\
\
```\
User clicks Add To Cart\
          ↓\
Find user's cart\
          ↓\
If cart doesn't exist → Create cart\
          ↓\
Check if product already exists\
          ↓\
If yes → Update quantity\
If no → Insert new cart item\
          ↓\
Redirect to Cart Page\
```\
\
Your current `CartDAO` has:\
\
```java\
boolean createCart(int userId);\
```\
\
It only returns **true/false**.\
\
But after creating the cart, the servlet needs the **new cart_id** to insert into `cart_items`.\
\
So `createCart()` is not enough.\
\
---\
\
# I recommend one improvement\
\
Let's improve `CartDAO` **before** writing the servlet.\
\
We'll add one method:\
\
```java\
int createAndReturnCart(int userId);\
```\
\
or\
\
```java\
Cart createCart(int userId);\
```\
\
This allows us to immediately know the new `cart_id`.\
\
---\
\
## Why?\
\
Without it, the servlet becomes messy because we'd have to:\
\
```\
createCart(userId);\
\
↓\
\
getCartByUserId(userId);\
\
↓\
\
getCartId();\
\
↓\
\
addToCart();\
```\
\
That's two database queries instead of one.\
\

# Phase 4: Shopping Cart Module\
\
This should include:\
\
```text\
1. CartServlet.java\
2. cart.jsp\
3. cart.css\
4. Add To Cart Functionality\
5. Update Quantity\
6. Remove Item\
7. Cart Total\
```\
\
This page should support:\
\
- ✅ Add product to cart\
- ✅ Display all cart items\
- ✅ Update quantity\
- ✅ Remove product\
- ✅ Calculate subtotal\
- ✅ Calculate grand total\
- ✅ Continue Shopping\
- ✅ Proceed to Checkout\
\
This is one of the core features of an e-commerce website.\
\
---\
\
# Before We Start\
\
We **should not** jump directly into `CartServlet.java`.\
\
There is **one missing connection** in our project.\
\
Currently, on the Product Details page, the **\\"Add To Cart\\"** button doesn't submit any data. If we create the Cart page now, there will be no way to add products into it.\
\
So the correct sequence is:\
\
```text\
Phase 4 : Shopping Cart\
\
Step 1 → Connect Add To Cart button\
Step 2 → CartServlet.java\
Step 3 → cart.jsp\
Step 4 → cart.css\
Step 5 → Update Quantity\
Step 6 → Remove Product\
Step 7 → Cart Total\
```\
\
This is the same sequence followed in real e-commerce applications.\
\
---\
\
# Step 1 : Modify `product-details.jsp`\
\

\

\
        \u003c% } %\u003e\

# 📌 Why we're doing this first\
\
If we build `cart.jsp` before connecting the **Add To Cart** button, the cart will always be empty. By wiring the button to submit the selected variant and quantity, the Cart module will immediately have real data to display.\

# Step 1 : Create `ProductDetailsServlet.java`\
\
## Create this file here\
\
```text\
FashionStore\
└── src\
    └── main\
        └── java\
            └── com.fashionstore\
                └── controller\
                    └── ProductDetailsServlet.java\
```\
\
---\
\
## Paste this code\
\
```java\
package com.fashionstore.controller;\
\
import java.io.IOException;\
import java.util.List;\
\
import com.fashionstore.dao.impl.ProductDAOImpl;\
import com.fashionstore.dao.impl.ProductVariantDAOImpl;\
import com.fashionstore.model.Product;\
import com.fashionstore.model.ProductVariant;\
\
import jakarta.servlet.ServletException;\
import jakarta.servlet.annotation.WebServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServlet;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;\
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;\
\
@WebServlet(\\"/product\\")\
public class ProductDetailsServlet extends HttpServlet {\
\
    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;\
\
    private ProductDAOImpl productDAO;\
    private ProductVariantDAOImpl variantDAO;\
\
    @Override\
    public void init() throws ServletException {\
\
        productDAO = new ProductDAOImpl();\
        variantDAO = new ProductVariantDAOImpl();\
\
    }\
\
    @Override\
    protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest request,\
            HttpServletResponse response)\
            throws ServletException, IOException {\
\
        String id = request.getParameter(\\"id\\");\
\
        if (id == null) {\
\
            response.sendRedirect(\\"products\\");\
            return;\
\
        }\
\
        int productId = Integer.parseInt(id);\
\
        Product product = productDAO.getProductById(productId);\
\
        List\u003cProductVariant\u003e variants =\
                variantDAO.getVariantsByProduct(productId);\
\
        request.setAttribute(\\"product\\", product);\
        request.setAttribute(\\"variants\\", variants);\
\
        request.getRequestDispatcher(\\"/WEB-INF/views/product-details.jsp\\")\
               .forward(request, response);\
\
    }\
\
}\
```\

## ❌ Problem\
\
Your `products.jsp` is in the wrong location.\
\
Currently your project looks like this:\
\
```text\
WEB-INF\
   └── views\
        ├── partials\
        │     ├── navbar.jsp\
        │     └── footer.jsp\
        │\
        └── home.jsp\
\
products.jsp   ❌ Outside WEB-INF/views\
```\
\
See in your screenshot, `products.jsp` is directly under `webapp`, not inside `WEB-INF/views`.\
\
That's why Eclipse is showing errors for:\
\
```jsp\
\u003c%@ include file=\\"partials/navbar.jsp\\" %\u003e\
```\
\
because there is **no `partials` folder beside `products.jsp`**.\
\
---\
\
# ✅ Solution (Recommended)\
\
Move `products.jsp` into the `views` folder.\
\
It should become:\
\
```text\
src\
└── main\
    └── webapp\
        └── WEB-INF\
            └── views\
                ├── home.jsp\
                ├── products.jsp   ✅\
                └── partials\
                    ├── navbar.jsp\
                    └── footer.jsp\
```\
\
After moving it, this include will work:\
\
```jsp\
\u003c%@ include file=\\"partials/navbar.jsp\\" %\u003e\
```\
\
and\
\
```jsp\
\u003c%@ include file=\\"partials/footer.jsp\\" %\u003e\
```\
\
---\
\
# 🚨 One More Problem I Found\
\
I also noticed this in your screenshot:\
\
```\
WEB-INF\
    └── lib\
```\
\
That **lib folder is unnecessary** in a Maven project.\
\
Since you're using Maven, all JARs come from `pom.xml`.\
\
We'll ignore it for now, but later we can remove it.\
\

\

            products.jsp\

                footer.jsp\

There are **two common MVC approaches**:\
\
### Option 1 (Recommended) ✅\
\
```\
HomeServlet\
      ↓\
WEB-INF/views/index.jsp\

\

\

HomeServlet\

WEB-INF/views/home.jsp\

\
URL:\
\

\

\
@WebServlet(\\"/home\\")\
public class HomeServlet extends HttpServlet {\
\
    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;\
\
    private CategoryDAOImpl categoryDAO;\
    private ProductDAOImpl productDAO;\
\
    @Override\
    public void init() throws ServletException {\
\
        categoryDAO = new CategoryDAOImpl();\
        productDAO = new ProductDAOImpl();\
\
    }\
\
    @Override\
    protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest request,\
                         HttpServletResponse response)\
            throws ServletException, IOException {\
\
        List\u003cCategory\u003e categories = categoryDAO.getAllCategories();\
\
        List\u003cProduct\u003e products = productDAO.getAllProducts();\
\
        request.setAttribute(\\"categories\\", categories);\
\
        request.setAttribute(\\"products\\", products);\
\
        request.getRequestDispatcher(\\"/WEB-INF/views/index.jsp\\")\
               .forward(request, response);\
\
    }\
\
}\
```\

### ⚠️ One small correction\
\
Earlier I asked you to create `navbar.jsp` and `footer.jsp` under:\
\
```text\
WEB-INF/views/partials\
```\
\
So **`index.jsp` should also be inside the `views` folder**, not directly under `webapp`.\
\
That means we'll use:\
\
```text\
WEB-INF\
   └── views\
          index.jsp\
          partials\
```\
\
This is a better MVC structure because users cannot access JSP files directly—they must go through the servlet.\

### My recommendation\
\

# Step 2: Verify Foreign Key Data\
\
### Products with Category\
\
```sql\
SELECT\
p.product_id,\
p.product_name,\
c.category_name,\
p.brand,\
p.price\
FROM products p\
INNER JOIN categories c\
ON p.category_id = c.category_id;\
```\
\
You should see all 40 products with their category names.\
\
---\
\
### Product Variants\
\
```sql\
SELECT\
p.product_name,\
pv.size,\
pv.stock\
FROM product_variants pv\
INNER JOIN products p\
ON pv.product_id = p.product_id;\
```\
\
You should see all variants with their product names.\
\
---\
\
### Cart Items\
\
```sql\
SELECT\
c.cart_id,\
u.full_name,\
p.product_name,\
pv.size,\
ci.quantity\
FROM cart_items ci\
JOIN cart c\
ON ci.cart_id = c.cart_id\
JOIN users u\
ON c.user_id = u.user_id\
JOIN product_variants pv\
ON ci.variant_id = pv.variant_id\
JOIN products p\
ON pv.product_id = p.product_id;\
```\
\
This checks that Cart → User → Product relationships are correct.\
\
---\
\
### Orders\
\
```sql\
SELECT\
o.order_id,\
u.full_name,\
o.total_amount,\
o.status,\
o.payment_method\
FROM orders o\
JOIN users u\
ON o.user_id = u.user_id;\
```\
\
---\
\
### Order Items\
\
```sql\
SELECT\
o.order_id,\
u.full_name,\
p.product_name,\
oi.quantity,\
oi.price\
FROM order_items oi\
JOIN orders o\
ON oi.order_id = o.order_id\
JOIN users u\
ON o.user_id = u.user_id\
JOIN product_variants pv\
ON oi.variant_id = pv.variant_id\
JOIN products p\
ON pv.product_id = p.product_id;\
```\

## Step 2: Create Tables\
\
Create a **new SQL tab** (`Ctrl + T`).\
\
Paste **only** this code.\
\
```sql\
USE fashion_store;\
\
CREATE TABLE users (\
    user_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,\
    full_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,\
    email VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL UNIQUE,\
    phone VARCHAR(15) NOT NULL UNIQUE,\
    password VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,\
    address VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,\
    city VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,\
    state VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,\
    pincode VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,\
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\
);\
\
CREATE TABLE categories (\
    category_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,\
    category_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL UNIQUE\
);\
\
CREATE TABLE products (\
    product_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,\
    category_id INT NOT NULL,\
    product_name VARCHAR(150) NOT NULL,\
    brand VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,\
    description TEXT NOT NULL,\
    price DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,\
    image_url VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,\
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,\
    CONSTRAINT fk_products_category\
        FOREIGN KEY (category_id)\
        REFERENCES categories(category_id)\
);\
\
CREATE TABLE product_variants (\
    variant_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,\
    product_id INT NOT NULL,\
    size VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,\
    stock INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\
    CONSTRAINT fk_variants_product\
        FOREIGN KEY (product_id)\
        REFERENCES products(product_id)\
);\
\
CREATE TABLE cart (\
    cart_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,\
    user_id INT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,\
    CONSTRAINT fk_cart_user\
        FOREIGN KEY (user_id)\
        REFERENCES users(user_id)\
);\
\
CREATE TABLE cart_items (\
    cart_item_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,\
    cart_id INT NOT NULL,\
    variant_id INT NOT NULL,\
    quantity INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\
    CONSTRAINT fk_cartitems_cart\
        FOREIGN KEY (cart_id)\
        REFERENCES cart(cart_id),\
    CONSTRAINT fk_cartitems_variant\
        FOREIGN KEY (variant_id)\
        REFERENCES product_variants(variant_id)\
);\
\
CREATE TABLE orders (\
    order_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,\
    user_id INT NOT NULL,\
    total_amount DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,\
    shipping_address VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,\
    payment_method VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,\
    status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PLACED',\
    order_date TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,\
    CONSTRAINT fk_orders_user\
        FOREIGN KEY (user_id)\
        REFERENCES users(user_id)\
);\
\
CREATE TABLE order_items (\
    order_item_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,\
    order_id INT NOT NULL,\
    variant_id INT NOT NULL,\
    quantity INT NOT NULL,\
    price DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,\
    CONSTRAINT fk_orderitems_order\
        FOREIGN KEY (order_id)\
        REFERENCES orders(order_id),\
    CONSTRAINT fk_orderitems_variant\
        FOREIGN KEY (variant_id)\
        REFERENCES product_variants(variant_id)\
);\
```\
\
### Execute\
\
- Press **Ctrl + Shift + Enter** (recommended), **or**\
- Click the **first lightning bolt (⚡)** to execute the entire script.\

# Interface 5: `CartDAO.java`\
\
Create the file:\
\
```text\
src/main/java\
└── com.fashionstore\
    └── dao\
        └── CartDAO.java\
```\
\
Copy and paste the following code:\
\
```java\
package com.fashionstore.dao;\
\
import com.fashionstore.model.Cart;\
\
public interface CartDAO {\
\
    // Create Cart\
    boolean createCart(int userId);\
\
    // Fetch Cart by User ID\
    Cart getCartByUserId(int userId);\
\
    // Fetch Cart by Cart ID\
    Cart getCartById(int cartId);\
\
    // Delete Cart\
    boolean deleteCart(int cartId);\
}\
```\
\
---\
\
## Why these methods?\
\
Our `cart` table stores **one cart per user** (`user_id` is `UNIQUE`).\
\
These methods cover:\
\
- Creating a cart for a new user.\
- Fetching a user's cart.\
- Fetching a cart by its ID.\
- Deleting a cart (useful in future if needed).\
\
\u003e **Note:** We are **not** adding methods like `addToCart()` or `updateQuantity()` here because those operations belong to the **`cart_items`** table, not the `cart` table.\
\
This separation follows good database design and the Single Responsibility Principle.\
\

### Small Design Note\
\
I deliberately separated `CartDAO` and `CartItemDAO`.\
\
- **CartDAO** → Manages the **cart** itself (one cart per user).\
- **CartItemDAO** → Manages the **items inside the cart** (add, update quantity, remove, total calculation).\
\
This mirrors your database design and keeps each interface focused on a single responsibility.\

## One Improvement (Recommended)\
\
I want to make **one architectural improvement** before we continue.\
\
Instead of writing separate methods like:\
\
```java\
getProductsByCategory(...)\
getProductsByPrice(...)\
getProductsByBrand(...)\
searchProducts(...)\
```\
\
we could create **one dynamic filter method**, for example:\
\
```java\
List\u003cProduct\u003e filterProducts(...);\
```\
\
This single method would combine:\
- Search\
- Category\
- Price\
- Brand\
- Sorting\
\
using one SQL query.\
\
### Pros\
- Less duplicate SQL.\
- Easier to maintain.\
- More scalable.\
\
### Cons\
- Slightly more complex SQL.\
\
### My Recommendation\
\
Since this is your **first full-stack project**, I recommend **keeping the separate methods** as shown above.\
\
The code will be easier to understand, debug, and explain during your viva or interview. Once you're comfortable with the basics, you can always refactor to a dynamic filtering approach later.\
\

## Why I want to do it this way\
\
We'll **first define the contract (interface)**, then implement it.\
\
For example:\
\
```java\
public interface UserDAO {\
    boolean registerUser(User user);\
}\
```\
\
Then:\
\
```java\
public class UserDAOImpl implements UserDAO {\
\
    @Override\
    public boolean registerUser(User user) {\
        // SQL Code\
    }\
}\
```\
\
This is exactly how the DAO pattern is intended to be used.\
\

## One More Improvement (Recommended)\
\
Since this is a complete Fashion Store application, I recommend **using `Optional\u003cT\u003e` only where it adds value** (for example, `getUserByEmail()`), but otherwise returning the model object or a `List\u003cModel\u003e` directly. This keeps the code easier to understand while still following good design practices.\

\

\

|-------|--------------------|\

| Products | getAllProducts(), searchProducts(), getProductsByCategory(), sortBy... |\

| Orders | getOrdersByUser(), getOrderItems() |\

# Option 1: Simple DAO Pattern (What I initially suggested)\
\
Structure:\
\
```text\
dao\

├── UserDAO.java\
├── ProductDAO.java\
├── CartDAO.java\
└── OrderDAO.java\

\

\
```java\
public class UserDAO {\
    public boolean registerUser(User user) {\
        ...\
    }\
}\
```\
\
### Pros\
- Fewer classes.\
- Easier to understand.\
- Very common in college projects.\
- Faster development.\

### Cons\
- Not as flexible.\
- Doesn't fully demonstrate programming to interfaces.\

# Option 2: Complete DAO Pattern (Industry Style)\
\
This is what you're referring to.\
\
Structure:\
\
```text\
src/main/java\
│\
└── com.fashionstore\
    │\
    ├── dao\
    │   ├── UserDAO.java          (Interface)\
    │   ├── ProductDAO.java\
    │   ├── CartDAO.java\
    │   └── OrderDAO.java\
    │\
    └── daoimpl\
        ├── UserDAOImpl.java\
        ├── ProductDAOImpl.java\
        ├── CartDAOImpl.java\
        └── OrderDAOImpl.java\
```\
\
Example:\
\
```java\
public interface UserDAO {\
\
    boolean registerUser(User user);\
\
    User login(String email, String password);\
}\
```\
\
Implementation:\
\
```java\
public class UserDAOImpl implements UserDAO {\
\
    @Override\
    public boolean registerUser(User user) {\
        ...\
    }\
}\
```\
\

# Why didn't I suggest this initially?\
\
Because I was optimizing for:\
- A college project.\
- Simplicity.\
- Fewer files.\
- Faster progress.\
\
Adding interfaces doubles the number of DAO-related files.\

Since you specifically said:\
- You want to learn properly.\
- You want to follow MVC.\
- You're building the project step by step.\

# Proposed Change (Major)\
\
### Current Structure\
\
```text\
dao\
│\
└── UserDAO.java\
```\
\
### Proposed Structure\
\
```text\
dao\
│\
├── UserDAO.java\
├── CategoryDAO.java\
├── ProductDAO.java\
├── ProductVariantDAO.java\
├── CartDAO.java\
├── CartItemDAO.java\
├── OrderDAO.java\
└── OrderItemDAO.java\
\
daoimpl\
│\
├── UserDAOImpl.java\
├── CategoryDAOImpl.java\
├── ProductDAOImpl.java\
├── ProductVariantDAOImpl.java\
├── CartDAOImpl.java\
├── CartItemDAOImpl.java\
├── OrderDAOImpl.java\
└── OrderItemDAOImpl.java\
```\
\
---\
\
# Pros\
\
- Follows the complete DAO design pattern.\
- Uses interfaces and implementation classes.\
- Easier to replace implementations later (for example, switching from MySQL to another database).\
- Better for interviews because you can explain dependency inversion and abstraction.\
- Matches enterprise Java architecture more closely.\
\
---\
\
# Cons\
\
- More classes to create.\
- Slightly more boilerplate code.\
- Takes a bit longer to develop.\
\
---\
\
# My Recommendation\
\
Since we're **still at the beginning of the project** (we've only completed the model layer), this is the **perfect time** to make this architectural decision.\
\
I recommend that we **adopt the complete DAO pattern** with:\
\
- `dao` → Interfaces\

package com.fashionstore.model;\

import java.math.BigDecimal;\
import java.sql.Timestamp;\
\
public class Product {\
\
    private int productId;\
    private int categoryId;\
    private String productName;\
    private String brand;\
    private String description;\
    private BigDecimal price;\
    private String imageUrl;\
    private Timestamp createdAt;\
\
    public Product() {\
    }\
\
    public Product(int productId, int categoryId, String productName, String brand,\
                   String description, BigDecimal price, String imageUrl,\
                   Timestamp createdAt) {\
        this.productId = productId;\
        this.categoryId = categoryId;\
        this.productName = productName;\
        this.brand = brand;\
        this.description = description;\
        this.price = price;\
        this.imageUrl = imageUrl;\
        this.createdAt = createdAt;\
    }\
\
    public int getProductId() {\
        return productId;\
    }\
\
    public void setProductId(int productId) {\
        this.productId = productId;\
    }\
\
    public int getCategoryId() {\
        return categoryId;\
    }\
\
    public void setCategoryId(int categoryId) {\
        this.categoryId = categoryId;\
    }\
\
    public String getProductName() {\
        return productName;\

## Why did I use `BigDecimal` for `price`?\
\
Our database column is:\
\
```sql\
price DECIMAL(10,2)\
```\
\
In Java, the recommended type for `DECIMAL` is `BigDecimal` because it avoids floating-point precision issues. This is a standard practice in Java applications.\

### Option 1 (Not Recommended)\
\
Create the class directly inside:\
\
```text\
com.fashionstore\
    └── User.java\
```\
\
This works, but after some time your package will contain:\
- User\
- Product\
- Category\
- Cart\
- Order\
- Servlets\
- DAOs\
- Utility classes\
\
Everything will be mixed together and difficult to manage.\

### Option 2 (Recommended) ✅\
\
Create a package named **`model`** inside `com.fashionstore`.\
\
Then create:\
\
```text\
com.fashionstore\
│\
├── controller\
├── dao\
├── model\
│   └── User.java\
└── util\
```\
\
This follows the **MVC design pattern**, which is what we've decided to use.\
\
### Why?\
\
- `model` → Contains only POJO/JavaBean classes.\
- `dao` → Contains database logic.\
- `controller` → Contains Servlets.\
- `util` → Contains utility classes like `DBConnection`.\
\
This keeps the project clean and organized.\
\
## My suggestion\
\
Since we're building this project from scratch and want to follow good practices, **create `User.java` inside the `model` package**, not directly under `com.fashionstore`.\
\

## Why this design?\
\
- Uses **camelCase** for Java fields (`userId`, `fullName`).\
- Matches the database columns (`user_id`, `full_name`) conceptually.\
- Includes:\
  - Default constructor\
  - Parameterized constructor\
  - Getters\
  - Setters\
\
This is the standard JavaBean/POJO style and works well with Servlets, JDBC, and JSP.\

```java\
package com.fashionstore.util;\
\
import java.sql.Connection;\
import java.sql.DriverManager;\
import java.sql.SQLException;\
\
public class DBConnection {\
\
    // Database URL\
    private static final String URL = \\"jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/fashion_store\\";\
\
    // Database Username\
    private static final String USERNAME = \\"root\\";\
\
    // Database Password\
    private static final String PASSWORD = \\"YOUR_PASSWORD\\";\
\
    // Method to establish database connection\
    public static Connection getConnection() {\
\
        Connection connection = null;\
\
        try {\
\
            // Load MySQL JDBC Driver\
            Class.forName(\\"com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver\\");\
\
            // Establish Connection\
            connection = DriverManager.getConnection(URL, USERNAME, PASSWORD);\
\
            System.out.println(\\"Database Connected Successfully...\\");\
\
        } catch (ClassNotFoundException e) {\
\
            System.out.println(\\"MySQL Driver Not Found\\");\
            e.printStackTrace();\
\
        } catch (SQLException e) {\
\
            System.out.println(\\"Database Connection Failed\\");\
            e.printStackTrace();\
\
        }\
\
        return connection;\
    }\
}\
```\

### 1. About the `filter` package\
\
There is **no problem** with skipping it.\
\
The `filter` package is typically used for features like:\
- Preventing users from accessing protected pages without logging in.\
- Session validation.\
- Authentication checks.\
\
For example:\
- A user shouldn't open `profile.jsp` without logging in.\
- A user shouldn't access `checkout.jsp` directly.\
\
These are handled by an `AuthFilter`.\
\

\
So, for now, your packages can simply be:\

\

\

│\

\
## Yes, JSP files **can** be inside `WEB-INF`.\
\
However, **they cannot be accessed directly by the browser**.\
\
For example, if you have:\
\
```text\
src/main/webapp\
│\
├── WEB-INF\
│   └── views\
│       └── login.jsp\
```\
\
Then this URL **will NOT work**:\
\
```text\
http://localhost:8080/FashionStore/WEB-INF/views/login.jsp\
```\
\
Tomcat blocks direct access to anything inside `WEB-INF`.\
\
Instead, the request flow is:\
\
```text\
Browser\
   │\
   ▼\
LoginServlet\
   │\
   ▼\
request.getRequestDispatcher(\\"/WEB-INF/views/login.jsp\\")\
       .forward(request, response);\
```\
\
The servlet forwards the request to the JSP, and the user never accesses the JSP directly.\
\
---\
\
## If you put JSPs outside `WEB-INF`\
\
For example:\
\
```text\
src/main/webapp\
│\
├── views\
│   ├── login.jsp\
│   ├── register.jsp\
│   └── products.jsp\
```\
\
Then the user can directly type:\
\
```text\
http://localhost:8080/FashionStore/views/login.jsp\
```\
\
and the page opens.\
\
This is simpler and very common for college projects.\
\
---\
\
# My Recommendation for Your Project\
\
Since we're building this from scratch and it's a **JSP/Servlet college project**, I recommend:\
\
```text\
src/main/webapp\
│\
├── assets\
│   ├── css\
│   ├── js\
│   └── images\
│\
├── views\
│   ├── auth\
│   ├── product\
│   ├── cart\
│   ├── order\
│   └── user\
│\
└── WEB-INF\
    └── web.xml\
```\
\
So:\
- `WEB-INF` contains only `web.xml` (and any future configuration files).\
- All JSPs go inside the `views` folder.\
- CSS, JavaScript, and images stay in `assets`.\
\
This gives you a clean structure while keeping JSPs easy to access during development.\
\

## Option 1: Keep all JSPs directly inside `src/main/webapp` (Simple)\
\
```text\
src/main/webapp\
│\
├── assets\
│   ├── css\
│   ├── js\
│   └── images\
│\
├── WEB-INF\
│\
├── index.jsp\
├── register.jsp\
├── login.jsp\
├── products.jsp\
├── product-details.jsp\
├── cart.jsp\
├── checkout.jsp\
├── order-success.jsp\
├── orders.jsp\
├── order-details.jsp\
└── profile.jsp\
```\
\
### Pros\
- Very easy to navigate.\
- Good for college projects.\
- Simpler servlet forwarding.\
\
### Cons\
- As the project grows, the `webapp` folder becomes crowded.\
\
---\
\
## Option 2: Organize JSPs into folders (More Professional)\
\
```text\
src/main/webapp\
│\
├── assets\
│   ├── css\
│   ├── js\
│   └── images\
│\
├── auth\
│\
├── product\
│\
├── cart\
│\
├── order\
│\
├── user\
│\
├── WEB-INF\
│\
└── index.jsp\
```\
\
Later, the JSPs would be placed inside their respective folders:\
- `auth` → Login, Register\
- `product` → Products, Product Details\
- `cart` → Cart, Checkout\
- `order` → Orders, Order Details, Order Success\
- `user` → Profile\
\
### Pros\
- Better organized.\
- Easier to maintain in larger projects.\
- Common in professional applications.\

**Proposed Change:**\
Inside `src/main/webapp`, instead of placing all JSP files directly in the root, organize them into folders.\
\

\

│   └── product-details.jsp\

│\

│   └── order-success.jsp\
│\
├── user\
│   └── profile.jsp\
│\
└── index.jsp\
```\
\

- Cleaner project structure.\
- Easier to locate JSP files.\
- Better scalability as the project grows.\
- Matches how many enterprise Java web applications organize views.\
\
### Cons\
- Servlet forwarding paths become slightly longer (for example, forwarding to `product/products.jsp` instead of `products.jsp`).\

# One Recommendation\
\
Since this is a **college project**, we can simplify it a little.\
\
Instead of creating all **8 packages** immediately, I recommend starting with **4 core packages**:\
\
```text\
com.fashionstore\
│\
├── controller\
├── dao\
├── model\
└── util\
```\
\
As we build features, we can add `filter`, `listener`, `exception`, and `constants` only when they're actually needed.\
\
### Why?\
\
- Cleaner project initially.\
- Less clutter.\
- Easier to learn.\
- We won't create empty packages that aren't used.\
\
I recommend this incremental approach because it keeps the project simple while still following the MVC architecture. ## One Recommendation (Approval Required)\
\
I would like to propose **one small change** to your `pom.xml`.\
\
### Current `pom.xml`\
\
It contains only:\
\
```xml\
\u003cgroupId\u003ecom.fashionstore\u003c/groupId\u003e\
\u003cartifactId\u003eFashionStore\u003c/artifactId\u003e\
\u003cversion\u003e0.0.1-SNAPSHOT\u003c/version\u003e\

\
### Proposed Change\
\
Add the dependencies we'll need:\
\
- Jakarta Servlet API\
- Jakarta JSP API\
- JSTL\
- MySQL Connector/J\
\
### Reason\
\
Without these dependencies:\
- JDBC classes won't be available through Maven.\
- Servlet and JSP APIs won't be managed by Maven.\
- We'll eventually need to add JARs manually or face compilation issues.\
\
### Pros\
\
- Cleaner project.\
- Easier dependency management.\
- Easy to share the project.\
- Standard Maven approach.\
\
### Cons\
\
- Maven will download a few dependencies from the internet the first time.\
- The `pom.xml` becomes slightly longer.\

\
That's how **foreign keys** work in MySQL.\
\
Your `cart_items` table has this foreign key:\
\
```sql\
FOREIGN KEY (cart_id)\
REFERENCES cart(cart_id)\
```\
\
So, before MySQL creates `cart_items`, the `cart` table **must already exist**.\
\
The correct creation order is:\
\
1. ✅ `users`\
2. ✅ `categories`\
3. ✅ `products`\
4. ✅ `product_variants`\
5. ✅ `cart`\
6. ✅ `cart_items`\
7. ✅ `orders`\
8. ✅ `order_items`\
\
If you try to create `cart_items` before `cart`, MySQL doesn't know what `cart(cart_id)` refers to, so it throws:\
\
\u003e **Error Code: 1824: Failed to open the referenced table 'cart'**\
\
So there was **nothing wrong with your `cart_items` query**. It was simply a dependency issue.\
\
I'm glad you found it yourself—that's exactly the kind of debugging experience that helps when working with relational databases.\

## One thing I would like to change (needs your approval)\
\
I recommend adding **one line before every `CREATE TABLE`**:\
\
```sql\
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS order_items;\

\
### Reason\
This allows you to rerun the script as many times as you want without manually dropping tables.\
\
### Pros\
- Easier development.\
- No \\"table already exists\\" errors.\
- One-click execution.\
\
### Cons\
- It deletes all existing data every time you run the script.\

    size VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,\
    stock INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\
    CONSTRAINT fk_variants_product\
        FOREIGN KEY (product_id)\
        REFERENCES products(product_id)\
);\
\
CREATE TABLE cart (\
    cart_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,\
    user_id INT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,\
    CONSTRAINT fk_cart_user\
        FOREIGN KEY (user_id)\
        REFERENCES users(user_id)\
);\
\
CREATE TABLE cart_items (\
    cart_item_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,\
    cart_id INT NOT NULL,\
    variant_id INT NOT NULL,\
    quantity INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\
    CONSTRAINT fk_cartitems_cart\
        FOREIGN KEY (cart_id)\
        REFERENCES cart(cart_id),\
    CONSTRAINT fk_cartitems_variant\
        FOREIGN KEY (variant_id)\
        REFERENCES product_variants(variant_id)\
);\
\
CREATE TABLE orders (\
    order_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,\
    user_id INT NOT NULL,\
    total_amount DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,\
    shipping_address VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,\
    payment_method VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,\
    status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PLACED',\
    order_date TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,\
    CONSTRAINT fk_orders_user\
        FOREIGN KEY (user_id)\
        REFERENCES users(user_id)\
);\
\
CREATE TABLE order_items (\
    order_item_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,\
    order_id INT NOT NULL,\
    variant_id INT NOT NULL,\
    quantity INT NOT NULL,\
    price DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,\
    CONSTRAINT fk_orderitems_order\
        FOREIGN KEY (order_id)\
        REFERENCES orders(order_id),\
    CONSTRAINT fk_orderitems_variant\
        FOREIGN KEY (variant_id)\
        REFERENCES product_variants(variant_id)\
);\

\
### Current Design\

### Proposed Design\
`product_variants` will contain:\
- variant_id\
- product_id\
- size\
- stock\

- M\
- L\
- XL\
\
This keeps the database simpler.\
\

- Simpler database design.\
- Easier SQL queries.\
- Easier Servlets and DAO classes.\
- Less complexity in the cart and order modules.\
\
### Cons\
- If you later want one product with multiple colors, you'll need separate product records.\
\

I **recommend** this approach for your college project.\

The **\\"Cons\\"** section explains what you might lose or what extra work is introduced if we adopt a proposed change. It doesn't mean the change is bad—it simply highlights the trade-offs.\
\
Let's use the example we discussed.\
\
---\
\
# Example: Proposed Change\
\
**Proposal:**\
Instead of storing `size` and `color` in the `products` table, create a separate `product_variants` table.\
\
---\
\
## Pros\
\
### 1. Supports multiple sizes\
\
Example:\
\
**Product:** Nike T-Shirt\
\
Available Sizes:\
- S\
- M\
- L\
- XL\
\
With a `product_variants` table, you can store all these sizes without duplicating the product.\
\
---\
\
### 2. Supports multiple colors\
\
Example:\
\
**Nike T-Shirt**\
\
Available Colors:\
- Black\
- White\
- Blue\
\
Again, all colors can be linked to the same product.\
\
---\
\
### 3. Better database design\
\
The product information (name, description, brand) is stored once, while the variations (size, color, stock) are stored separately.\
\
---\
\
# Cons\
\
## 1. One extra table\
\
### Without `product_variants`\
\
You have only:\
\
- Products\
- Categories\
- Users\
- Cart\
- Orders\
\
Simple structure.\
\
---\
\
### With `product_variants`\
\
You now have:\
\
- Products\
- Product Variants\
- Categories\
- Users\
- Cart\
- Orders\
\
One more table means more database objects to manage.\
\
---\
\
## 2. More complex SQL queries\
\
### Without `product_variants`\
\
To display a product:\
\
```sql\
SELECT * FROM products;\
```\
\
Very simple.\
\
---\
\
### With `product_variants`\
\
You may need to combine data from two tables:\
\
```sql\
SELECT p.product_name,\
       pv.size,\
       pv.color,\
       pv.stock\
FROM products p\
JOIN product_variants pv\
ON p.product_id = pv.product_id;\
```\
\
This is more complex because you have to use a `JOIN`.\
\
---\
\
## 3. More backend code\
\
### Without variants\
\
When the user clicks **Add to Cart**, you only store:\
\
- Product ID\
- Quantity\
\
---\
\
### With variants\
\
You must also store:\
\
- Product ID\
- Selected Size\
- Selected Color\
- Quantity\
\
That means your Servlets, DAO classes, and JSPs need extra logic to handle size and color selection.\
\
---\
\
## 4. More time to develop\
\
For a college project, adding variants means:\
\
- Creating another table\
- Writing additional SQL\
- Updating more Java classes\
- Handling more user input\
\
So, it increases development time.\
\
---\
\
# Simple Comparison\
\
### Without Variants (Simple)\
\
**Products Table**\
\
| Product | Size | Color |\
|----------|------|--------|\
| Nike T-Shirt | M | Black |\
\
If you also want **L** and **White**, you'd have to create separate rows or accept that each product only has one size and one color.\
\
---\
\
### With Variants (Better Design)\
\
**Products Table**\
\
| Product ID | Product |\
|------------|---------|\
| 101 | Nike T-Shirt |\
\
**Product Variants Table**\
\
| Variant ID | Product ID | Size | Color |\
|------------|------------|------|--------|\
| 1 | 101 | M | Black |\
| 2 | 101 | L | Black |\
| 3 | 101 | M | White |\
| 4 | 101 | L | White |\
\
One product can now have many size and color combinations without repeating the product details.\

# I have one suggestion before we freeze this\
\
The `products` table currently has `color` and `size` as columns. This works if each product has only one size and one color.\
\
However, in a fashion store, a single product often comes in **multiple sizes** (S, M, L, XL) and **multiple colors** (Black, White, Blue).\
\
For example:\
\
**Classic T-Shirt**\
- Sizes: S, M, L, XL\
- Colors: Black, White, Navy\
\
If we keep `size` and `color` directly in the `products` table, we'd have to duplicate the product for every size/color combination.\
\
A more scalable design would introduce a separate table, often called `product_variants`, to store combinations like size, color, stock, and price if needed.\
\

\
**Do you want to support multiple sizes and colors for a product (like a real fashion store), or do you want to keep the database simpler by assuming one size and one color per product?**\

## One suggestion before we move to the database\
\
I recommend we spend one more step on **application flow** before creating tables.\
\
The order would be:\
\
- ✅ **Milestone 1:** Pages (Completed)\
- ⏳ **Milestone 2:** User navigation and module flow\
- ⏳ **Milestone 3:** Database design\
- ⏳ **Milestone 4:** Maven project structure\
- ⏳ **Milestone 5:** UI development\
- ⏳ **Milestone 6:** Backend development\
\
The reason is that once we define how the user moves from page to page, the database entities become much easier to identify, and we avoid creating unnecessary tables.\
\
So, before we write a single SQL statement, we'll answer questions like:\
- Which pages require the user to be logged in?\
- What happens after clicking **Add to Cart**?\
- What happens if the cart is empty?\
- What data flows from **Cart → Checkout → Order Success**?\
- When is the database updated?\
\
Once that flow is finalized, the database design becomes straightforward and much cleaner.
